In general, casting a variable to a list type will only work if the actual data type of the variable is a list or a subtype of list. If the variable type is not compatible with the desired list type, a ClassCastException will be thrown.

To avoid this error, you can try to use the following code instead:

```
val names = document.get("name") as List<String>
val quantities = document.get("quantity") as List<Int>
val expenses = document.get("expenses") as List<Double>
```

By casting the arrays to a read-only List type instead of a MutableList, you can ensure that the data types match and prevent any potential ClassCastException errors from occurring.
